_ruling_memory_floor_gb.ruling: 14.0 STANDS, UNCONVERTED. Ruled by the dafoam-supervisor 2026-09-06. This section is written so the question is not re-litigated by the next reader: the earlier _open_question flagged a unit gap that DOES NOT EXIST IN THE CODE.
_ruling_memory_floor_gb.which_constant: The frozen document registers two memory constants and neither is named memory_floor_gb. sec.2 line 91-92 inherits MEM_LIMIT = 8g -- the container --memory cap, i.e. what the run is ALLOWED to consume -- and MEMAVAIL_FLOOR_GIB = 14.0 (not lowered), the host MemAvailable floor a stage must see before it starts. The schema's memory_floor_gb is the hold criterion at queue_runner.py:932, which is the MemAvailable semantic. So 14.0 is the right constant and 8g is not.
_ruling_memory_floor_gb.the_unit_gap_is_a_NAMING_defect_not_a_VA: MEASURED at scripts/queue_runner.py:195-200. mem_available_gb() reads MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo -- which is in kB -- and returns int(kB) / (1024.0 * 1024.0). Dividing kB by 1024 squared yields GiB, NOT GB. The function name, the field name memory_floor_gb and the runner's own log line at :943 ('MemAvailable %.1f GB < registered floor %s GB') all say GB; the arithmetic says GiB. THE FIELD NAME IS WRONG AND THE SEMANTICS ARE RIGHT.
_ruling_memory_floor_gb.therefore: 14.0 in this field is compared against a GiB quantity, and is therefore EXACTLY the registered MEMAVAIL_FLOOR_GIB = 14.0 of cases/dafoam/curriculum_D12/d12r_grade.py:50. No conversion is needed and none is correct.
_ruling_memory_floor_gb.what_converting_would_have_done: Converting 14.0 GiB to 15.03 GB would have OVER-ASKED THE RUNNER BY 7.4 % (15.03 / 14.0 = 1.0736) against a quantity that was already in GiB. That is not a safe rounding: it is a change to a registered figure, made by this lane's arithmetic, in the tightening direction -- and it would have held the entry on a floor the pre-registration never registered.
_ruling_memory_floor_gb.the_earlier_draft_had_the_direction_back: The superseded _open_question_memory_floor_gb said 14.0 GB is SMALLER than 14.0 GiB and so 'asks for slightly LESS headroom than the document registers.' That reasoning assumed the runner compares in GB. It does not. There is no weakening and there was never anything to correct.

_THE_53_OF_53_IS_A_FINDING_AND_NOT_A_TIC.AND_A_SECOND_DEFECT_IN_THE_SAME_NINE_LIN: Launcher line 1197 read: say "  [backtick]cp -a[backtick] preserves mtimes, ...". BACKTICKS INSIDE DOUBLE QUOTES ARE COMMAND SUBSTITUTION, so PRINTING THAT REFUSAL EXECUTED cp -a with no operands -- the 'cp: missing file operand' in launcher.queue.out:15 -- and emitted the message with the words cp -a REPLACED BY THE COMMAND'S EMPTY STDOUT (launcher.queue.out:17 begins '   preserves mtimes'). Now single-quoted and driven: the line prints cp -a literally and runs nothing. IT SURVIVED BECAUSE cp WITH NO OPERANDS FAILS LOUDLY AND CHANGES NOTHING; a quoted span naming a command that DOES something would have injected its effect and left no scar. THAT ASYMMETRY IS THE LESSON, and it is why markdown and shell strings are written through QUOTED heredocs.
